new: "Only primates have opposable thumbs" means if you have them, you are a primate. It does not mean every primate has them. Think of "only members can use the pool": that does not mean every member uses the pool. So the passage does not promise lemurs their thumbs, but it does not take them away either. Nothing says any lemur lacks them, so this answer has no support and does not have to be true.

new: The passage says all higher primates are thought to have evolved from a single diurnal species of lower primates. This tells us the ancestral species was diurnal, but it does not tell us that all current higher primates are diurnal. Evolution from a diurnal ancestor does not guarantee that all descendants remain diurnal. Many higher primate species could have evolved nocturnal habits over millions of years. The passage provides no information about the current activity patterns of higher primates as a group, only about their evolutionary origin.
